name: Doria's Hawk
rangeDescription: New guinea, including and batanta (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A large, inconspicuous raptor of lowlands and foothill forest interior. Brown back and long tail with strong barring, pale underparts with strong sparse streaking, pale eye-brow and a thick dark eye-stripe.

name: Black Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Highlands of malay peninsula and western sumatra
description: The otherwise solidly dark plumage of this laughingthrush is punctuated by a patch of bare bluish-gray skin behind the eye and a bright orange-red bill. Favors the lower levels of foothill and submontane broadleaved forests; often in pairs or small flocks, sometimes mixed in with other species.

name: Unicolored Antwren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (northern rio de janeiro to far northern rio grande do sul)
description: Uncommon small, short-tailed antwren of the lower and middle levels of humid forests. Very active and often follows mixed-species flocks.

name: Sumba Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Lowlands of sumba island (western lesser sundas)
description: A green pigeon with striking yellowish markings and edgings on the wing. Male has a chestnut lower back, while the back of the female is entirely green.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Black-chested Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid highlands of southwestern mexico (jalisco to western oaxaca)
description: Very handsome but rather local sparrow endemic to interior southwest Mexico. Found in scrubby woodland and edge of dry tropical foothills and interior valleys.

name: Jameson's Antpecker
rangeDescription: Eastern congo and northern democratic republic of the congo to western uganda and western tanzania
description: A small, slender-billed, warbler-like waxbill with pinkish-brown legs and different-looking sexes: the male has a red forehead, dull brown upperparts, and a rusty-chestnut face and underparts, while the female has a tawny-brown face and cheeks, pale buff underparts with scattered dark chevrons, and dull brown upperparts. Pairs and small groups forage by themselves or in mixed-species flocks, in the understory and middle levels of primary, secondary, and gallery forest, often near water.

name: Violet Crow
rangeDescription: Southern moluccas (seram, buru, and ambon)
description: An entirely blackish short-tailed crow. Has a subtle purplish sheen that is visible in only certain lighting conditions.

name: Riverside Wren
rangeDescription: Pacific lowlands of southwestern costa rica and far western panama
description: Medium-sized wren with rufous upperparts and bold black-and-white barred underparts. Complex black-and-white face pattern.

name: Snares Snipe
rangeDescription: Snares islands (northeast, broughton, and alert stack)
description: A small, stocky wader endemic to New Zealand. Dark brown and black, with barred feathers on the belly.

name: Regent Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Southeastern queensland to southern and central victoria; southeastern south australia
description: Medium-sized honeyeater found in dry forests of northeastern Victoria and seasonally in small numbers up the eastern coast to around Brisbane. Critically endangered and the focus of a recovery program.

name: Cajamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Andes of northern peru (cajamarca)
description: Small antpitta with a restricted range in the western Andes of northwestern Peru. Note the chestnut brown plumage and pale belly; like other antpittas, it has long legs and a short tail.

name: Olive-streaked Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Foothills and highlands of costa rica and western panama (to chiriquí and ngäbe-buglé)
description: Small, fruit-eating flycatcher found in lower to middle levels of humid forest. Most common in the mountains, but occasionally seen in lowland areas.

name: Red-and-white Spinetail
rangeDescription: Far southeastern colombia to eastern peru and amazonian brazil
description: Strikingly bicolored spinetail, bright rusty above and white below. Note the dusky lores.

name: Roraiman Nightjar
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southeastern venezuela, adjacent northern brazil, and guyana
description: A medium-sized, dark nightjar of tepui highlands, difficult to identify by plumage alone. Cryptically patterned with dark brown and gray accented with buffy and whitish bars and spots.
imageCreditName: Jhonathan Miranda - Wandering Venezuela Birding Expeditions

name: Pemba Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Pemba (off northeastern tanzania)
description: A medium-sized, chunky pigeon that has an olive-green back and a gray head and underparts. Flight is fast and direct.

name: Golden-backed Bishop
rangeDescription: Scrub of coastal angola; são tomé
description: A small, short-tailed, huge-billed bishop. Breeding males are beautiful birds, mostly black with a yellow-orange back.

name: Golden-crowned Brushfinch
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of central peru (san martín southward to western cusco in the apurímac valley), also local on outlying ridges (cordillera azul, southwestern loreto; cerros del sira, huánuco)
description: This chunky bird is dingy yellow below and dark brownish above with a yellow crown. Sexes similar.

name: Splendid Sunbird
rangeDescription: Senegal to sierra leone, eastward to southern nigeria, cameroon, central african republic, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and southwestern south sudan; nonbreeding visitor to northeastern gabon
description: A fairly large, long-billed sunbird in which males and females are very different. Males are dark, with an iridescent multi-colored hood and a black belly.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Spot-winged Monarch
rangeDescription: New guinea, including raja ampat islands (off western new guinea), and louisiade archipelago (off southeastern new guinea)
description: A small to medium-sized bird of lowland and foothill forest interior. Slate-gray above with white spots in the wing, white below, black face and silver-gray bill.

name: Ecuadorian Seedeater
rangeDescription: Mountains of southwestern colombia (nariño) to northern peru (cajamarca)
description: Scarce and very local. A rather plain, easily overlooked, small seed-eating bird.
